phases.name: absent
phases.note: Non-breeding visitor: curve months May to August are near zero (0.00 to 0.01) in CR. Derived from the activity curve, not a dated source. Arrival in September and departure in April are partial months.

vocalizations.description: Harsh, inharmonious chattering given by both sexes during combative encounters and in alarm; not stated as seasonal in the source.

external.note: iNaturalist id 9346 (Wikidata P3151) agrees with the iNaturalist taxa API; checked 2026-11-01.

conservation.note: IUCN least concern via Wikidata P141 = Q211005.

range.note: Wikipedia: breeds in the Nearctic (south to central Mississippi and northern Georgia), winters mainly in Central America and northern South America, as far north as Mexico. Country list transcribed from that prose; Caribbean and Venezuela are listed in the range note and map caption.

traits.mass_kg.note: BodyMass-Value 32.83 g (Dunning 2008, as recorded in EltonTraits), converted to kg.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia gives a body weight range of 22.3 to 42 g (CRC Handbook of Avian Body Masses, 1992, cited there); converted to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the Wikipedia length range 17 to 22 cm. Not an averaged measurement.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the Wikipedia wingspan range 23 to 32 cm. Not an averaged measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Mean lifespan under a constant-hazard approximation: -1 / ln(S) with S = 0.534 apparent annual adult survival (Scholer row X=202; MAPS, United States, SE 0.042). 1 / 0.6273 = 1.59, rounded to 1.6. Apparent survival is biased low where emigration occurs, and the value excludes first-year mortality, so it is a lower-bound proxy. Wikipedia's 11 years 7 months maximum and 14-year captive age are not used.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 60, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Nect 20 (percent, certainty A), converted to fractions. Wikipedia's prose (insects, berries, nectar) agrees.

traits.social.note: Solitary outside the mating season, per Wikipedia. group_size [1,2] is a judgement for pairs; winter roosting groups are not quantified here.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal = 0. Wikipedia describes daytime foraging and singing. Diurnal is a classification from those two sources.

traits.defense.note: judgement: passerine default of fleeing to cover; not stated in a source.

traits.wariness.note: judgement: moderate wariness for a canopy songbird; no source value.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat: ground 30 percent; understory 10, mid-high 20 and canopy 40 percent summed to arboreal 70 percent.

habitat.resources.note: Weights follow the EltonTraits diet split. Wikipedia names insects, fruit (dark ripe fruit), nectar and feeders. Shelter and perch tags are judgement for a canopy songbird.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia: now often in orchards, farmland, urban parks and suburban landscapes; attracted to feeders. Adapter is a judgement from that description.

vocalizations.note: Wikipedia describes the warning chatter in combative confrontations. Season and time window are judgement; no seasonal restriction is stated.

look.note: judgement: block model colours and proportions from the male plumage in Wikipedia (orange underparts and shoulder, black head and back).

seasonal.phases.note: Window read from the CR activity curve (near-zero May to August). Derived from observation counts, which are a proxy for presence.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs: passerine bird. Wikipedia: 'fairly long legs' on a sturdy body.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop for branch and ground movement and Fly for migration and short catching flights. Wikipedia says they 'clamber, hover, and hang among foliage'. Climb and Hover have no pose in this kit, so clambering is approximated by the hop pose.

traits.perching.note: Passerine: Wikipedia calls it a passerine, and it perches in trees.

traits.flight.note: Wikipedia: a medium-sized passerine that migrates between North America and the Neotropics. Class-level trait for a passerine songbird.

traits.skin.note: Wikipedia: a medium-sized passerine that migrates between North America and the Neotropics. Class-level trait for a passerine songbird.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Wikipedia: a medium-sized passerine that migrates between North America and the Neotropics. Class-level trait for a passerine songbird.

traits.respiration.note: Wikipedia: a medium-sized passerine that migrates between North America and the Neotropics. Class-level trait for a passerine songbird.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Wikipedia: a medium-sized passerine that migrates between North America and the Neotropics. Class-level trait for a passerine songbird.

traits.size_class.note: Validator bound: mass under 0.05 kg is Tiny (mass 0.03283 kg).

habitat.shelter_tag.note: judgement: generic shelter tag for roosting in canopy cover. Wikipedia does not name a roost structure.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: breeds in the Nearctic and winters mainly in Central America and northern South America, which is a migration strategy. The CR curve confirms a non-breeding winter pattern.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia describes eggs, nestlings and fledglings, and independence after fledging. Stage durations are not stated and are omitted.

behavior.note: Authored species-local program bt-icterus-galbula-v1 in behavior.json. It omits nesting and song because the supported CR region is non-breeding, and it selects the nearest insect, fruit or nectar food. Shared perching-songbird program not used: its nesting months 3 to 6 and single invertebrate food tag do not fit the CR calendar or diet.
